slides.title: Why do skates feel slower on cold mornings?
slides.sub: What to change in your wheels, bearings and warm up

slides.title: Cold wheels grip less
slides.body: Cold urethane stiffens and the contact patch shrinks, so your wheel behaves like a harder grade than the one printed on it.

slides.title: Why the first corner catches you out
slides.caption: The same wheel grips less when cold, because its contact patch shrinks.

slides.title: Cold oil drags at first
slides.body: Thick bearing oil gives a short roll for the first few minutes. Do not judge your bearings on a cold morning, and do not flood them with oil.

slides.title: Watch for dew you cannot see
slides.body: Painted lines, tiles, metal covers and shade stay damp after the road looks dry. Scout your first lap slowly.

slides.title: Skate your grippier compound
slides.body: If you own XFirm and XXFirm sets, the cold morning call is XFirm. It buys back some grip, not all of it.

slides.title: Double the warm up
slides.body: Start it off the skates and keep hard efforts for the back half. See a physiotherapist or doctor for sharp pain, swelling or pain that lasts days.
